descriptions.description: Host plant, biology and habitat. Copaifera langsdorffii Desf., perhaps also C. marginata Benth. — Cerrado, transition to riparian and Atlantic forest, disturbed vegetation around cultures, parks.

Description. Adult. Colouration. Dark brown to almost black (Fig. 105). Head, pronotum and mesopraescutum with pattern consisting of fine whitish or yellowish lines, mesoscutum only with longitudinal lines. Ocelli reddish. Antennal segments 3 – 5 yellow to brown with dark tips. Clypeus whitish. Metapleura orange or yellow. Tibiae and tarsi yellow. Forewing (Fig. 123) transparent, colourless with smaller or larger dark brown or black dots around radular spinules in cells r 1, r 2, m 1, m 2 and cu 1 as well as at apex of clavus, sometimes almost absent; veins yellow or light brown with brown tips. Hindwing whitish, transparent, clavus slightly infuscate. Abdomen with two longitudinal submedian rows of whitish dots; intersegmental membranes yellow or orange. Young specimens orange or brown getting gradually darker with age. Structure. Head inclined in a 30 ° angle from longitudinal body axis. Genal processes irregularly narrowing towards blunt apex, 0.4 – 0.6 times as long as vertex along midline (Fig. 114). Antenna 2.7 – 3.1 times as long as head width. Rostrum short, only apical segment visible in profile, 0.4 times as long as head width. Forewing (Fig. 123) 2.5 – 3.1 times as long as head width, 1.9 – 2.5 times as long as wide, broadly, irregularly rounded apically, most strongly curved in cell r 2; pterostigma moderately long, broad at base, about as wide as adjacent part of cell r 1; cell cu 1 0.8 – 1.0 times higher than wide; surface spinules present in all cells but much reduced, usually present in apical half of cell r 1, in the middle of cells r 2, m 1, m 2 and cu 1 along wing margin, and in cell cu 2 leaving broad spinule-free stripes along the veins, more robust and more expanded on pigmented areas. Metatibia 0.5 – 0.6 times as long as head width. Terminalia as in Figs 130, 144, 145, 160. Male proctiger 0.4 times as long as head width, with narrow, slightly curved posterior lobes basally. Paramere simple, lamellar, slender in apical third; apex ending in a single small, forward directed slerotised tooth; inner surface sparsely covered in long setae. Distal segment of aedeagus expanded in apical third, consisting of a distal oval dilatation and a proximal tooth; sclerotised end tube of ductus ejaculatorius short, almost straight. Female proctiger 1.3 – 1.4 times as long as head width, dorsal outline very weakly sinuous, apex obliquely truncate; circumanal ring 0.2 – 0.3 times as long as proctiger. Female subgenital plate 0.5 – 0.6 times as long as proctiger, apex pointed. Measurements (in mm; 6 ♂, 7 ♀). Head width ♂ 0.78 – 0.86, ♀ 0.76 – 0.96; antenna length ♂ 2.34 – 2.70, ♀ 2.22 – 2.76; forewing length ♂ 1.98 – 2.34, ♀ 2.26 – 2.48; male proctiger length 0.32 – 0.36; paramere length 0.32 – 0.34; length of distal segment of aedeagus 0.32 – 0.34; female proctiger length 1.04 – 1.20. Fifth instar immature (Figs 109, 110). Colouration. Dirty whitish. Apices of flagellar segments brown. Sclerites on head and thorax dirty yellowish. Head and thoracic tergites with orange dots. Wing pads and legs yellowish grey. Abdomen with one median and each a sublateral row of orange dots on each segment, dorsally. Structure. Body 1.3 – 1.5 times as long as wide. Antenna 9 - segmented, often division of segment 8 and 9 incomplete, 1.8 – 2.2 times as long as forewing pad. Marginal setae on forewing pad weakly capitate, particularly the longer ones, long and medium long, the longer setae mostly longer than distance between bases of adjacent setae; setae on dorsum of wing pads pointed (Fig. 169). Circumanal ring large, strongly indented anteriorly (Fig. 172). Measurements (in mm) and ratios (7 immatures). Body length 1.42 – 1.64, antenna length 1.04 – 1.22.

Comments. Mitrapsylla copaiferae differs from other copaiba psyllids as indicated in the key. It is morphologically similar to M. compta and M. fumipennis in the short genal processes, the forewing which is slightly angled in cell r 2, the simple, long and slender paramere and the long female terminalia. It differs from the former in the slightly longer genal processes, the absence of a continuous submarginal band on the forewing, the apically narrower paramere, the distal portion of the aedeagus which is strongly inflated and the female proctiger with the dorsal outline slightly more indented subapically. From the latter it differs in the forewing membrane which is colourless rather than infuscate, the apically narrower paramere and the longer apical dilatation of the aedeagus. Based on the short genal processes, the weakly angular forewing and details of the male and female terminalia, Mitrapsylla minuticonis Brown & Hodkinson from Panama is closely related to M. copaiferae. Its host plant is presently unknown, but we postulate that it is Copaifera.
Distribution. Brazil (GO, MG, MS, MT, SP).
Etymology. Noun in genitive case. Named after its host genus Copaifera.

Etymology. Noun in genitive case. Named after its host genus Copaifera.
Distribution. Brazil (GO, MG, MS, MT, SP).

Comments. Mitrapsylla copaiferae differs from other copaiba psyllids as indicated in the key. It is morphologically similar to M. compta and M. fumipennis in the short genal processes, the forewing which is slightly angled in cell r 2, the simple, long and slender paramere and the long female terminalia. It differs from the former in the slightly longer genal processes, the absence of a continuous submarginal band on the forewing, the apically narrower paramere, the distal portion of the aedeagus which is strongly inflated and the female proctiger with the dorsal outline slightly more indented subapically. From the latter it differs in the forewing membrane which is colourless rather than infuscate, the apically narrower paramere and the longer apical dilatation of the aedeagus. Based on the short genal processes, the weakly angular forewing and details of the male and female terminalia, Mitrapsylla minuticonis Brown & Hodkinson from Panama is closely related to M. copaiferae. Its host plant is presently unknown, but we postulate that it is Copaifera.

Description. Adult. Colouration. Dark brown to almost black (Fig. 105). Head, pronotum and mesopraescutum with pattern consisting of fine whitish or yellowish lines, mesoscutum only with longitudinal lines. Ocelli reddish. Antennal segments 3 – 5 yellow to brown with dark tips. Clypeus whitish. Metapleura orange or yellow. Tibiae and tarsi yellow. Forewing (Fig. 123) transparent, colourless with smaller or larger dark brown or black dots around radular spinules in cells r 1, r 2, m 1, m 2 and cu 1 as well as at apex of clavus, sometimes almost absent; veins yellow or light brown with brown tips. Hindwing whitish, transparent, clavus slightly infuscate. Abdomen with two longitudinal submedian rows of whitish dots; intersegmental membranes yellow or orange. Young specimens orange or brown getting gradually darker with age. Structure. Head inclined in a 30 ° angle from longitudinal body axis. Genal processes irregularly narrowing towards blunt apex, 0.4 – 0.6 times as long as vertex along midline (Fig. 114). Antenna 2.7 – 3.1 times as long as head width. Rostrum short, only apical segment visible in profile, 0.4 times as long as head width. Forewing (Fig. 123) 2.5 – 3.1 times as long as head width, 1.9 – 2.5 times as long as wide, broadly, irregularly rounded apically, most strongly curved in cell r 2; pterostigma moderately long, broad at base, about as wide as adjacent part of cell r 1; cell cu 1 0.8 – 1.0 times higher than wide; surface spinules present in all cells but much reduced, usually present in apical half of cell r 1, in the middle of cells r 2, m 1, m 2 and cu 1 along wing margin, and in cell cu 2 leaving broad spinule-free stripes along the veins, more robust and more expanded on pigmented areas. Metatibia 0.5 – 0.6 times as long as head width. Terminalia as in Figs 130, 144, 145, 160. Male proctiger 0.4 times as long as head width, with narrow, slightly curved posterior lobes basally. Paramere simple, lamellar, slender in apical third; apex ending in a single small, forward directed slerotised tooth; inner surface sparsely covered in long setae. Distal segment of aedeagus expanded in apical third, consisting of a distal oval dilatation and a proximal tooth; sclerotised end tube of ductus ejaculatorius short, almost straight. Female proctiger 1.3 – 1.4 times as long as head width, dorsal outline very weakly sinuous, apex obliquely truncate; circumanal ring 0.2 – 0.3 times as long as proctiger. Female subgenital plate 0.5 – 0.6 times as long as proctiger, apex pointed. Measurements (in mm; 6 ♂, 7 ♀). Head width ♂ 0.78 – 0.86, ♀ 0.76 – 0.96; antenna length ♂ 2.34 – 2.70, ♀ 2.22 – 2.76; forewing length ♂ 1.98 – 2.34, ♀ 2.26 – 2.48; male proctiger length 0.32 – 0.36; paramere length 0.32 – 0.34; length of distal segment of aedeagus 0.32 – 0.34; female proctiger length 1.04 – 1.20. Fifth instar immature (Figs 109, 110). Colouration. Dirty whitish. Apices of flagellar segments brown. Sclerites on head and thorax dirty yellowish. Head and thoracic tergites with orange dots. Wing pads and legs yellowish grey. Abdomen with one median and each a sublateral row of orange dots on each segment, dorsally. Structure. Body 1.3 – 1.5 times as long as wide. Antenna 9 - segmented, often division of segment 8 and 9 incomplete, 1.8 – 2.2 times as long as forewing pad. Marginal setae on forewing pad weakly capitate, particularly the longer ones, long and medium long, the longer setae mostly longer than distance between bases of adjacent setae; setae on dorsum of wing pads pointed (Fig. 169). Circumanal ring large, strongly indented anteriorly (Fig. 172). Measurements (in mm) and ratios (7 immatures). Body length 1.42 – 1.64, antenna length 1.04 – 1.22.
Host plant, biology and habitat. Copaifera langsdorffii Desf., perhaps also C. marginata Benth. — Cerrado, transition to riparian and Atlantic forest, disturbed vegetation around cultures, parks.

Copaifera langsdorffii Desf., C. marginata Benth., C. trapezifolia Hayne. — In the material at hand, 26 adult specimens (7 ♂, 19 ♀) are parasitised by Strepsiptera, consisting of 11 male pupae, two of which are hatched (Fig. 223), and 16 adult females (Fig. 224). In general each psyllid is parasitised by one strepsipteran but one female psyllid has two parasitoids, one ♂ pupa and an adult female. The parasitoids were always found in the abdomen. — Cerrado, Atlantic forest, Araucaria forest, riparian and transitional forests, natural and degraded, along plantations, single trees.

Description. Adult (Fig. 106). Colouration. Head (Fig. 6) brown, vertex orange basally; dirty whitish stripes present on either side of coronal suture longitudinally, along lateral margin of vertex obliquely and at base of genal processes transversely. Eyes and ocelli reddish. Antenna dark brown to black with bases of segments 3 – 8 light becoming increasingly shorter towards apex. Clypeus dirty yellowish in the middle, dark brown along the edges; rostrum yellow with black tip. Thorax reddish brown dorsally; pronotum and mesopraescutum along fore margin dark brown; one yellow longitudinal stripe on mesopraescutum and - scutum and each a submedian and sublateral longitudinal stripe on either side of mesoscutum; mesoscutellum yellow; metanotum almost black; thorax laterally and ventrally dark brown to black with some yellow patches laterally. Legs dark brown, tibiae and meso- and metatarsi yellow. Forewing (Fig. 125) transparent, colourless or yellow with dark areas of radular spinules in cells m 1, m 2 and cu 1 as well as at apex of clavus; veins yellow or light brown. Hindwing whitish, transparent. Abdomen brown, intersegmental membranes reddish orange. Often with white dots on head, thorax and abdomen arranged in a longitudinal pattern. Younger specimens with less expanded dark colour. Structure. Head inclined in a 45 ° angle from longitudinal body axis. Genal processes subconical with subacute apex, 0.4 – 0.6 times as long as vertex along midline (Figs 6, 116). Antenna 2.2 – 2.5 times as long as head width. Rostrum short, apical segment and sometimes apex of median segment visible in profile, 0.4 – 0.5 times as long as head width. Forewing (Fig. 125) 2.9 – 3.3 times as long as head width, 2.3 – 2.5 times as long as wide, broadly, evenly rounded apically; pterostigma short, about as wide as or wider than adjacent part of cell r 1 at base; cell cu 1 0.7 – 0.8 times higher than wide; surface spinules much reduced, present in apical half of cell r 1, in the middle of cells r 2, m 1, m 2 and cu 1 along wing margin, and in cell cu 2, leaving broad spinule-free stripes along the veins. Metatibia 0.7 – 0.8 times as long as head width. Terminalia as in Figs 131, 148 – 150, 162 and 167. Male proctiger 0.3 – 0.4 times as long as head width, with narrow, slightly curved posterior lobes basally. Paramere lamellar, widened along posterior margin near apex forming small lobe; with small, inwards directed sclerotised tooth apically which is narrowly truncate apically; inner surface moderately densely covered in long setae, with a dense group of thick spines at the hind margin subapically. Distal segment of aedeagus inflated in apical half; distal dilatation with apico-ventral hook which varies in size (Figs 149, 150), two apical small teeth, a lobe on either side subapically and a short membranous lobe basally; sclerotised end tube of ductus ejaculatorius short, very weakly curved. Female proctiger 0.9 – 1.0 times as long as head width, dorsal outline almost straight or weakly sinuous, apex slightly upturned, obliquely truncate; circumanal ring 0.3 times as long as proctiger. Female subgenital plate 0.5 – 0.6 times as long as proctiger, ventral outline almost straight; densely covered in setae, without seta-free patch in the middle on either side. Measurements (in mm) and ratios (5 ♂, 5 ♀). Head width ♂ 0.56 – 0.64, ♀ 0.56 – 0.66; antenna length ♂ 1.40 – 1.58, ♀ 1.26 – 1.50; forewing length ♂ 1.62 – 1.98, ♀ 1.68 – 2.16; male proctiger length 0.20 – 0.22; paramere length 0.20 – 0.22; length of distal segment of aedeagus 0.22 – 0.24; female proctiger length 0.60 – 0.64. Fifth instar immature. Colouration. White, antenna yellowish with apices of flagellar segments brown. Tibiae and tarsi greyish brown. Structure. Body 1.3 – 1.9 times as long as wide. Antenna 8 - segmented, 1.3 – 1.9 times as long as forewing pad. Marginal setae on forewing pad weakly capitate, short and medium long, mostly shorter than distance between bases of adjacent setae; setae on dorsum of wing pads weakly capitate. Circumanal ring small, weakly indented anteriorly (Fig. 173). Measurements (in mm) and ratios (23 immatures). Body length 1.00 – 1.90, antenna length 0.66 – 0.92.

Comments. Mitrapsylla gloriae differs from other copaiba psyllids as indicated in the key. In the small body size, moderately long, subacute genal processes, lamellar paramere and structure of the aedeagus, it resembles closely M. borealis, from which it differs in the paramere which is more expanded apically, the apical dilatation of the aedeagus, which is about half as long as distal segment, and the denser setae of the female subgenital plate, which cover the entire apical two thirds. The last instar immature differs from other Mitrapsylla species from copaiba in the relatively small, dorso-anteriorly weakly indented outer circumanal ring. We assume that the fourth instar immatures collected together with a longer series of fifth instar immatures of M. gloriae (sample D. Burckhardt & D. L. Queiroz # 142 (2 )) belong to this species though the circumanal ring has its largest longitudinal extension in the middle rather than sublaterally as in the last instar. For this reason we do not include the fourth instar specimens in the type series. The same sample comprises also material of Jataiba uncigera and M. copaiferae whose immatures are quite distinct. M. gloriae is widely distributed and very common on its host plants. The specimens from C. marginata are slightly smaller than those from C. langsdorffii but do not differ structurally.
Distribution. Brazil (DF, GO, MG, MS, MT, PR, RJ, SC, SP).
Etymology. Noun in genitive case. Dedicated to Gloria Queiroz for her help in the field at Fazenda Bainha.

Comments. Mitrapsylla gloriae differs from other copaiba psyllids as indicated in the key. In the small body size, moderately long, subacute genal processes, lamellar paramere and structure of the aedeagus, it resembles closely M. borealis, from which it differs in the paramere which is more expanded apically, the apical dilatation of the aedeagus, which is about half as long as distal segment, and the denser setae of the female subgenital plate, which cover the entire apical two thirds. The last instar immature differs from other Mitrapsylla species from copaiba in the relatively small, dorso-anteriorly weakly indented outer circumanal ring. We assume that the fourth instar immatures collected together with a longer series of fifth instar immatures of M. gloriae (sample D. Burckhardt & D. L. Queiroz # 142 (2 )) belong to this species though the circumanal ring has its largest longitudinal extension in the middle rather than sublaterally as in the last instar. For this reason we do not include the fourth instar specimens in the type series. The same sample comprises also material of Jataiba uncigera and M. copaiferae whose immatures are quite distinct. M. gloriae is widely distributed and very common on its host plants. The specimens from C. marginata are slightly smaller than those from C. langsdorffii but do not differ structurally.

Description. Adult (Fig. 106). Colouration. Head (Fig. 6) brown, vertex orange basally; dirty whitish stripes present on either side of coronal suture longitudinally, along lateral margin of vertex obliquely and at base of genal processes transversely. Eyes and ocelli reddish. Antenna dark brown to black with bases of segments 3 – 8 light becoming increasingly shorter towards apex. Clypeus dirty yellowish in the middle, dark brown along the edges; rostrum yellow with black tip. Thorax reddish brown dorsally; pronotum and mesopraescutum along fore margin dark brown; one yellow longitudinal stripe on mesopraescutum and - scutum and each a submedian and sublateral longitudinal stripe on either side of mesoscutum; mesoscutellum yellow; metanotum almost black; thorax laterally and ventrally dark brown to black with some yellow patches laterally. Legs dark brown, tibiae and meso- and metatarsi yellow. Forewing (Fig. 125) transparent, colourless or yellow with dark areas of radular spinules in cells m 1, m 2 and cu 1 as well as at apex of clavus; veins yellow or light brown. Hindwing whitish, transparent. Abdomen brown, intersegmental membranes reddish orange. Often with white dots on head, thorax and abdomen arranged in a longitudinal pattern. Younger specimens with less expanded dark colour. Structure. Head inclined in a 45 ° angle from longitudinal body axis. Genal processes subconical with subacute apex, 0.4 – 0.6 times as long as vertex along midline (Figs 6, 116). Antenna 2.2 – 2.5 times as long as head width. Rostrum short, apical segment and sometimes apex of median segment visible in profile, 0.4 – 0.5 times as long as head width. Forewing (Fig. 125) 2.9 – 3.3 times as long as head width, 2.3 – 2.5 times as long as wide, broadly, evenly rounded apically; pterostigma short, about as wide as or wider than adjacent part of cell r 1 at base; cell cu 1 0.7 – 0.8 times higher than wide; surface spinules much reduced, present in apical half of cell r 1, in the middle of cells r 2, m 1, m 2 and cu 1 along wing margin, and in cell cu 2, leaving broad spinule-free stripes along the veins. Metatibia 0.7 – 0.8 times as long as head width. Terminalia as in Figs 131, 148 – 150, 162 and 167. Male proctiger 0.3 – 0.4 times as long as head width, with narrow, slightly curved posterior lobes basally. Paramere lamellar, widened along posterior margin near apex forming small lobe; with small, inwards directed sclerotised tooth apically which is narrowly truncate apically; inner surface moderately densely covered in long setae, with a dense group of thick spines at the hind margin subapically. Distal segment of aedeagus inflated in apical half; distal dilatation with apico-ventral hook which varies in size (Figs 149, 150), two apical small teeth, a lobe on either side subapically and a short membranous lobe basally; sclerotised end tube of ductus ejaculatorius short, very weakly curved. Female proctiger 0.9 – 1.0 times as long as head width, dorsal outline almost straight or weakly sinuous, apex slightly upturned, obliquely truncate; circumanal ring 0.3 times as long as proctiger. Female subgenital plate 0.5 – 0.6 times as long as proctiger, ventral outline almost straight; densely covered in setae, without seta-free patch in the middle on either side. Measurements (in mm) and ratios (5 ♂, 5 ♀). Head width ♂ 0.56 – 0.64, ♀ 0.56 – 0.66; antenna length ♂ 1.40 – 1.58, ♀ 1.26 – 1.50; forewing length ♂ 1.62 – 1.98, ♀ 1.68 – 2.16; male proctiger length 0.20 – 0.22; paramere length 0.20 – 0.22; length of distal segment of aedeagus 0.22 – 0.24; female proctiger length 0.60 – 0.64. Fifth instar immature. Colouration. White, antenna yellowish with apices of flagellar segments brown. Tibiae and tarsi greyish brown. Structure. Body 1.3 – 1.9 times as long as wide. Antenna 8 - segmented, 1.3 – 1.9 times as long as forewing pad. Marginal setae on forewing pad weakly capitate, short and medium long, mostly shorter than distance between bases of adjacent setae; setae on dorsum of wing pads weakly capitate. Circumanal ring small, weakly indented anteriorly (Fig. 173). Measurements (in mm) and ratios (23 immatures). Body length 1.00 – 1.90, antenna length 0.66 – 0.92.

Host plant, biology and habitat. Copaifera langsdorffii Desf., C. marginata Benth., C. trapezifolia Hayne. — In the material at hand, 26 adult specimens (7 ♂, 19 ♀) are parasitised by Strepsiptera, consisting of 11 male pupae, two of which are hatched (Fig. 223), and 16 adult females (Fig. 224). In general each psyllid is parasitised by one strepsipteran but one female psyllid has two parasitoids, one ♂ pupa and an adult female. The parasitoids were always found in the abdomen. — Cerrado, Atlantic forest, Araucaria forest, riparian and transitional forests, natural and degraded, along plantations, single trees.
